slides.title: 3 milky coffees that look alike
slides.subtitle: Same espresso, different milk. Can you tell which is which?

slides.title: Macchiato: a mark of milk
slides.body: Macchiato means "marked" or "stained" in Italian. It is espresso with just a small dollop of milk foam on top, so it is the most espresso-forward of the three.
slides.highlight: A dollop of foam, not a cup of milk.

slides.title: Cortado: espresso, cut with milk
slides.body: Cortado comes from the Spanish for "cut". Steamed milk cuts the espresso at roughly equal parts, with no thick foam layer on top.

slides.title: Cappuccino: the milkiest one
slides.body: Espresso, steamed milk and a thick layer of foam. The extra milk makes it sweeter, thicker and creamier than the other two.

slides.title: Least to most milk
steps: Macchiato: espresso with a dollop of foam
Cortado: about half milk, no thick foam
Cappuccino: steamed milk and thick foam

slides.title: Foam, half, or full milk
slides.body: Macchiato gets a dollop, cortado half, cappuccino the most milk.
